name: Phillip T. (Terry) Ragon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Phillip Ragon, known as Terry, founded InterSystems, a software company that enables hospitals and banks to analyze big data, in 1978.
Ragon retains full ownership of the company, which generates around $1 billion in annual sales.
Ragon and his wife, Susan, joined the Giving Pledge in 2017.
After a trip to South Africa in 2009 where Terry and Susan saw the ravages of AIDS, they established the Ragon Institute to pursue an HIV vaccine.
The couple announced a $200 million gift to endow the Ragon Institute of Massachusetts General Hospital, MIT and Harvard in 2019.
forbes_facts: Ragon spent his high school senior year in Bogota, Colombia and has donated over half a million dollars since 2013 to a religious school there.
Ragon is the son of a U.S. Air Force fighter pilot.

name: Kwon Hyuk-bin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Kwon Hyuk-bin founded Smilegate in 2002 and has built it into one of the most successful gaming companies in South Korea.
Following a 2008 partnership with Chinese internet giant Tencent, it released its most popular title, CrossFire.
Through his Smilegate Foundation, Kwon has established schools in China and Vietnam, providing education in IT, among other subjects.
forbes_facts: Kwon's first venture in business was an ill-fated educational software company that he founded but soon tanked.
While in college, Kwon was selected into Samsung's prestigious software program for students.

name: Joe Lonsdale
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Joe Lonsdale is the managing partner of venture capital firm 8VC, which he cofounded in 2015 and relocated to Texas in 2020.
8VC, with $6 billion in assets, has made several big bets on startups in defense tech and life sciences.
A serial entrepreneur, Lonsdale has also cofounded data mining firm Palantir, which went public in 2020, and government software firm OpenGov.
After studying computer science at Stanford, Lonsdale started his career working for billionaire investor Peter Thiel's hedge fund.
In 2018 he founded the Cicero Institute, a conservative think tank that advocates for entrepreneur-friendly public policy in healthcare, housing and other causes.

name: Fabrizio Di Amato
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Fabrizio Di Amato is the founder and chairman of Rome, Italy-based Maire, a publicly traded engineering and renewable energy firm.
He founded Maire at age 19 in 1983 with only three employees and grew it through acquisitions including the purchases of Fiat Engineering in 2004 and Tecnimont in 2005.
Di Amato took the company public on the Milan stock exchange in 2007; he now owns 51% of the shares.
Maire operates more than 1,500 engineering plants in 45 countries around the world.

name: Ted Turner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Ted Turner is best known for founding CNN, the first 24-hour news station, in 1980.
After his father died in 1963, Turner took control of his father's billboard company, Turner Advertising, and rebranded it "Turner Broadcasting."
He sold Turner to Time Warner for $7.3 billion in stock in 1996 and saw his fortune tumble when Time Warner bought AOL in 2001, causing shares to drop.
Turner is America's third-largest individual landowner, with roughly 2 million acres.
Turner, a Giving Pledge signee, chairs the Turner Foundation Inc, which is dedicated to protecting and restoring America's natural environments.
forbes_facts: Turner owns a more than 30,000-acre estate in Florida called Avalon Plantation, where he married actress Jane Fonda in 1991.
Turner sold St. Phillips Island, his private island off of South Carolina, to the state in a charitable transfer in 2017. The land is now part of a state park.

name: Qian Dongqi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Qian Dongqi is the founder and chairman of Ecovacs Robotics, one of China's largest makers of vacuum cleaner robots.
It also supplies robotic window washers, air purifiers and lawn mowers.
Qian worked with state-owned organizations in international business and imports and exports before setting up Ecovacs in 1998.
He took the company public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2018.
His son and heir-apparent, David Cheng Qian, is vice chairman of the company.
forbes_facts: Qian holds a master's degree in Philosophy.

name: Fernando Roig
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Fernando Roig owns ceramics firm Pamesa as well as a 9% stake in Spanish supermarket chain Mercadona.
His billionaire brother Juan Roig is the majority shareholder of Mercadona, which was founded by their parents in 1977.
Juan and Fernando took over Mercadona with their sisters in 1981 when it was only an eight-store chain.
Since then they have turned it into one of Europe's largest food retailers, with nearly 1,700 supermarkets and 110,000 employees.
Fernando also owns professional soccer team Villarreal C.F. of Spain.
forbes_facts: Fernando's sister-in-law, Hortensia Herrero (married to his brother Juan), also helped build Mercadona and is a billionaire.

name: Hans Georg Naeder
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Hans Georg Naeder heads orthopedic device maker Ottobock SE; it takes its name from his grandfather Otto Bock, who founded the business in 1919.
The company, which had its IPO in 2025, is a partner with the Paralympics since 1988, producing hockey sledges and custom prosthetics for skiers, snowboarders and sprinters.
Since taking the reins from his father at age 28, Hans Georg has expanded the staff more than seven-fold to over 10,000 worldwide.
Ottobock operates sales and service branches in 60 countries and generates annual revenue of over $1.6 billion.
Swedish private equity firm EQT took a 20% stake in Ottobock in June 2017; Naeder and his family bought back the stake in March 2024.
forbes_facts: An avid sportsman, Hans Georg helmed his 46-meter sailing yacht Pink Gin to victory in the New Zealand Millennium Cup in 2007. He owns Baltic Yachts of Finland.
Residing in Duderstadt, Germany, he is divorced and has two daughters. In 2019, he received the German Federal Cross of Merit for achievements in the medical field.

name: Hiroshi Ishibashi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Hiroshi Ishibashi is a grandson of the founder of Bridgestone, the world's second-largest tire maker by revenue.
He owns a small but valuable stake in the Tokyo-listed company but does not hold any executive position.
Hiroshi heads the Ishibashi Foundation, which operates Tokyo's Bridgestone Museum of Art.

name: Rishad Naoroji
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Rishad Naoroji is the low-profile cousin of  billionaires Adi Godrej, Nadir Godrej, Jamshyd Godrej and Smita Crishna-Godrej.
Naoroji had a one-fifth share of the Godrej family assets until 2024 when their storied Godrej group was split into two factions.
After the split, stock exchange filings show that Naoroji sold his stakes in group companies to his cousins.
The wildlife enthusiast and photographer has never been involved in the business.
He founded the Raptor Research and Conservation Foundation to focus on the conservation of Asian birds of prey.

name: Luis Enrique Yarur Rey
name_chinese: 路易斯·恩里克·亚鲁·雷伊
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Luis Enrique Yarur Rey is the chairman of Banco de Credito e Inversiones (BCI), a Chilean retail and commercial bank.
BCI has nearly 200 branches throughout Chile, Peru and Florida.
The bank was founded by the Yarur family in 1937. Today, it is one of Chile's largest banking institutions, with more than $80 billion in assets.
In 2015, BCI purchased City National Bank of Florida for $947 million; it was the first time a Chilean bank purchased a U.S. financial institution.

name: Liang Feng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Liang Feng is a cofounder and the chairman of Shanghai Putailai New Energy Technology, a supplier of components and machinery to the lithium-ion battery industry.
Putailai's clients include Samsung and LG.
Liang holds an undergraduate degree in automation from South China University of Technology.
He also holds a master's degree in economics from Zhejiang University.
